candidates.name: Reaction stoichiometry
candidates.definition: Using mole ratios from a balanced equation to relate amounts of reactants and products by mass, moles, solution volume or gas volume.
candidates.include: Tag when an amount of one substance must be calculated from another through a balanced equation.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag when the stoichiometry is part of a titration (tag titration-analysis) or electrolysis (tag electrolysis-faraday) unless it is a separate requested calculation.

candidates.name: Limiting reactant and yield
candidates.definition: Identifying the limiting reactant, calculating theoretical yield and excess reactant remaining, and calculating percent yield.
candidates.include: Tag when the student must decide which reactant limits the reaction, or compute theoretical, actual or percent yield.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag single-reactant stoichiometry with an obvious excess stated.

candidates.name: Enthalpy of reaction
candidates.definition: The enthalpy change of a reaction as written, its sign, and how it scales with the amount reacting in a thermochemical equation.
candidates.include: Tag when heat released or absorbed must be calculated from ΔH and an amount of reactant, or ΔH related to a balanced equation.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag bond-enthalpy, formation-enthalpy or Hess's-law calculations unless ΔH scaling to an amount is also required.

candidates.name: Moles, molar mass and particle counts
candidates.definition: Converting among mass, moles and number of particles using molar mass and Avogadro's number, including counting atoms within a formula.
candidates.include: Tag when the student must perform or reason about a mass-mole-particle conversion that is a substantive step, or the question is about the mole itself.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag when a mole conversion is an unremarkable first step of a larger stoichiometry, gas or solution calculation already captured by another concept, unless the question isolates it.

candidates.name: Bond enthalpies
candidates.definition: Estimating ΔH of a reaction as the energy of bonds broken minus the energy of bonds formed, and explaining energy changes as bond breaking (endothermic) and formation (exothermic).
candidates.include: Tag when average bond enthalpies are used to estimate ΔH, or bonds broken and formed must be counted.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag bond-length comparisons (tag bond-order).

candidates.name: Calorimetry and specific heat
candidates.definition: Using q = mcΔT, heat capacity and calorimeter data to determine heat transferred or the enthalpy change of a process, and evaluating calorimetry procedures and errors.
candidates.include: Tag when calorimetry data or q = mcΔT must be used, or a calorimetry procedure or error analyzed.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag phase-change heat (q = nΔH) alone (tag phase-change-energy).

candidates.name: Endothermic and exothermic processes
candidates.definition: Identifying processes as endothermic or exothermic from temperature observations, the sign of q or ΔH, or energy diagrams, keeping system and surroundings distinct.
candidates.include: Tag when the direction of heat flow or the sign of ΔH must be determined from evidence or an energy diagram.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag energy profiles with activation barriers (tag activation-energy).

candidates.name: Standard enthalpies of formation
candidates.definition: Calculating ΔH°rxn as the sum of ΔHf° of products minus reactants, with elements in their standard states assigned zero.
candidates.include: Tag when ΔHf° values are used or a formation reaction must be identified.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag Hess's-law manipulations of non-formation equations (tag hess-law).

candidates.name: Hess's law
candidates.definition: Finding the enthalpy change of a target reaction by reversing, scaling and adding equations with known ΔH, because enthalpy is a state function.
candidates.include: Tag when equations must be manipulated and combined to obtain ΔH, or path independence is explained.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag the analogous manipulation of K values (tag k-manipulation).

candidates.name: Particle diagrams of reactions
candidates.definition: Using particle-level drawings of reactants and products that conserve atoms and are consistent with the balanced equation, including showing limiting and excess reactants.
candidates.include: Tag when a particulate representation of a reaction must be drawn, chosen or interpreted.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag numerical stoichiometry with no particle representation.

candidates.name: Writing and balancing chemical equations
candidates.definition: Writing balanced chemical equations from descriptions or observations so that atoms are conserved, with correct formulas, coefficients and phases.
candidates.include: Tag when the student must write or balance an equation that is not a net ionic or redox half-reaction equation.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag when a balanced equation is given; use net-ionic-equations or redox-half-reactions for those equation types.

candidates.name: Ideal gas law
candidates.definition: Using PV = nRT and its proportionalities (Boyle, Charles, Avogadro) to calculate or predict gas quantities, including gas density and molar mass.
candidates.include: Tag when a gas variable must be calculated or a P-V-T-n relationship predicted.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag partial-pressure reasoning alone (tag partial-pressures) or kinetic-theory explanations (tag kinetic-molecular-theory).

candidates.name: Molarity and solution preparation
candidates.definition: Calculating and using molar concentration (moles of solute per liter of solution), including preparing a solution of a target concentration.
candidates.include: Tag when molarity must be calculated, or moles found from molarity and volume as a substantive step.
candidates.exclude: Molality and percent-by-mass concentrations are not assessed (tag colligative-properties if present); dilution belongs to dilution.
